questions.q: When may you cross a broken lane line?
options: Only at night
When the road is clear, for example to overtake or change lane
At any time, even when the road isn't clear
Never
questions.explain: You may cross a broken line (sign 801) when the road is clear, to overtake, change lane or comply with the law.

questions.q: What is forbidden at a double continuous white separation line?
options: Crossing it with the whole vehicle or part of it, from either side
Crossing it only from the right
There's no restriction, it's decoration only
Crossing it only during daytime
questions.explain: A double continuous separation line (803) forbids the vehicle from crossing, wholly or partly, in either direction.

questions.q: A road is marked with a double line: the line closer to your lane is broken, and the far line is continuous. May you cross to overtake, when the road is clear?
options: Permitted only for a heavy vehicle
No, crossing is forbidden entirely
Permitted only on a non-urban road
Yes, you may cross from the side where the line closer to you is broken
questions.explain: On a double line, you check the line closer to your lane: if it's broken, you may cross when the road is clear, even if the far line is continuous.

questions.q: What does a continuous yellow line at the side of the road mark, where there's no kerb?
options: A public transport lane
A pedestrian crossing
A stop line
The edge of the carriageway; you drive to its left and don't cross to its right except in certain circumstances
questions.explain: A continuous yellow line (807) marks the edge of the carriageway; you drive on its left-hand side and don't cross to its right, except to avoid an accident or a delay, or to comply with the law.

questions.q: What does a white block line on the road mark?
options: A bicycle crossing
A dedicated lane - an exclusive turn, acceleration, deceleration or weaving lane
A stop line
An area where parking is forbidden
questions.explain: A white block line (808) marks a dedicated lane; you drive in it according to the lane's purpose, not the lane you were in before.

questions.q: Where must you stop when there's a duty to stop at a junction?
options: There's no fixed line, it's at the driver's discretion
Exactly before the stop line
After the stop line, inside the junction
Anywhere convenient before the junction
questions.explain: A stop line (810) marks exactly where a vehicle must stop when there's a duty to stop - at a red light, at a stop sign, or before a railway crossing.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the white triangles painted on the road before a stop line, known as give-way markings?
options: To show a mandatory turning direction
To mark a cycle lane
To warn from a distance that you must give way, even before you see the sign
To mark a parking place
questions.explain: Give-way markings warn an approaching driver that they must give way, even before they notice the sign itself.

questions.q: A wide pedestrian crossing spanning the road is split into two. Which half do you cross in?
options: The right-hand half
Anywhere you choose
The left-hand half
Exactly in the middle
questions.explain: A pedestrian crossing (811) split into two halves - you cross in its right-hand half.

questions.q: What is forbidden on a traffic island marked in white on the road?
options: Driving over it, stopping on it or parking on it
There's no restriction, it's decorative marking only
Only parking on it, but stopping is allowed
Only stopping on it, but parking is allowed
questions.explain: A traffic island marked in white (815) must not be driven over, stopped on or parked on.

questions.q: A lane is marked with a white arrow showing a right turn only, ahead of the junction. What must you do?
options: Continue straight ahead, because the arrow is only a recommendation
Ignore the arrow if there's no traffic light
Choose any convenient direction
Enter the junction and cross it only in the direction shown by the arrow marked in the lane
questions.explain: A white arrow in a lane (813) is binding: you enter the junction and cross it only in the direction marked in the lane you entered from.

questions.q: What is permitted on the side of the road where the kerb is painted red-white?
options: Paid parking
No stopping or parking, unless needed to comply with the law
Free parking without restriction
A short stop only
questions.explain: A red-white kerb forbids all stopping and parking, unless needed to comply with the law - exactly like sign 433.

questions.q: What does a kerb painted alternately blue-white indicate?
options: Parking permitted for a fee
An absolute stopping prohibition
Stopping for an authorised vehicle only
Highlighting only, with no parking restriction
questions.explain: A blue-white kerb marks parking permitted for a fee, under sign 439 placed beside it.

questions.q: What does a kerb painted red-yellow indicate?
options: Stopping forbidden for every vehicle, except the type of vehicle allowed by the sign, and only to pick up or drop off passengers
Highlighting a traffic island, without restriction
A parking prohibition at night only
Paid parking for any vehicle
questions.explain: A red-yellow kerb forbids stopping by every vehicle, except the type of vehicle allowed by the sign above it, and only to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.q: What does a kerb painted black-white indicate?
options: Highlighting and emphasis only - not a parking prohibition
Parking permitted for a fee
An absolute parking prohibition
Stopping for a public transport vehicle only
questions.explain: A black-white kerb is meant only to highlight pavements, dividers and built traffic islands, and doesn't set a parking prohibition.

questions.q: A kerb in grey, with no clear official paint. What does this mean for parking?
options: An absolute parking prohibition, like red-white
Parking permitted only for disabled drivers
Paid parking, like blue-white
There's no such kerb colour in the regulations in Israel; the rule follows a sign if there is one, or otherwise the ordinary rules
questions.explain: There's no grey kerb colour recognised in the regulations in Israel - that's a common misconception. A kerb that hasn't been painted at all says nothing by itself.

questions.q: What must you do at a red light?
options: Only slow down, without stopping
Stop only if there's another vehicle at the junction
Stop before the stop line
Speed up to cross before it turns fully on
questions.explain: A red light requires a full stop before the stop line or the traffic light, and you must not cross until the light changes.

questions.q: What does red and amber together mean?
options: You must stop only if you see traffic at the junction
You may already move off with care
You're still stopped as at red, but getting ready to drive off with the green
The light is about to change to flashing red
questions.explain: Red and amber together - you continue to stop as at red, but this is preparation for the green that's about to appear.

questions.q: What is true about a flashing amber light on a traffic light?
options: You must make a full stop in every case
It only appears on a expressway
It is completely identical to a red light
You proceed with care under the ordinary rules; this is the only light that doesn't override a priority sign
questions.explain: A flashing amber light permits proceeding with care under the ordinary rules; it's the only light that doesn't override a sign setting priority (reg. 22(b)).

questions.q: The pedestrian signal shows a red figure, and the pedestrian is already in the middle of the road. What should they do?
options: Stop in the middle of the road and wait
Complete the crossing at once
Sit down and wait for a vehicle to stop
Go back at once to the side they came from
questions.explain: A red pedestrian figure forbids starting to cross; anyone already on the road must complete the crossing at once.

questions.q: Above a lane on a busy road, a signal shows a red X. What does it mean?
options: You must move into this lane at once
The lane is open for driving
You must not drive in the lane above which the signal is shown
The lane is for bicycles only
questions.explain: A red X above a lane (sign 723, lane closed) forbids driving in that lane, until an open lane (724) is shown or until the next junction.

questions.q: A vehicle approaches a railway crossing where a double flashing red light is on, and there's no stop line or barrier. At what minimum distance from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop?
options: {{fact:rail.stop_distance_min_m}}
Ten metres
One metre
There's no fixed minimum distance
questions.explain: When there's no stop line and no barrier, you must stop at least {{fact:rail.stop_distance_min_m}} from the nearest rail (reg. 56).

questions.q: A police officer stands at a junction and extends one arm parallel to the direction of traffic, palm open. What does the signal mean?
options: Go
Turn left
Stop
Slow down only
questions.explain: Extending one arm, or both, parallel to the direction of traffic, palm open, is the go signal (reg. 24(a)).

questions.q: A police officer raises a hand with an open palm towards your direction of travel. What must you do?
options: Move off with care
Turn right
Sound the horn and wait for a further instruction
Stop
questions.explain: A raised hand with an open palm facing the direction of traffic is the stop signal - you must stop (reg. 24(a)).

questions.q: A signal given by a police officer directing traffic partly overlaps with a sign at the junction, but isn't fully identical to it. Which instruction prevails?
options: Whoever reached the junction first chooses
The police officer's instruction, even if it contradicts the sign
Neither of them, you must act only under the general rule
The sign, because it was placed in advance
questions.explain: A road user must obey a police officer's instruction even when it contradicts the regulations, signs or other traffic instructions (reg. 23(b)).

questions.q: A municipal traffic warden in uniform, who is authorised, gives a traffic instruction at a junction. Must you obey them?
options: Only during daytime
No, only a police officer has that authority
Only if they're wearing green uniform
Yes, the instruction is binding exactly like a police officer's
questions.explain: A municipal traffic warden authorised by the police district commander or the head of the traffic division may give traffic instructions, and you must obey them (reg. 23(a)(1)).
